paragraphs.title: The Lord Appears and Judges the Land

answers: Samaria and Jerusalem
Egypt and Babylon
Edom and Moab
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says that Micah saw the word concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
easy.q: Concerning which two places did Micah see his prophecy?

answers: Only the kings of Judah
All ye people, the earth, and all that is therein
Only the inhabitants of Jerusalem
easy.explanation: Verse 2 calls all people, the earth, and everything in it to hearken.
easy.q: Who is called to hear the Lord’s testimony?

answers: They rise higher
They disappear from the earth
They are molten

easy.q: What happens to the mountains when the Lord appears?

answers: He is a witness against the people
He leads Judah’s army
He builds Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The Lord GOD is called to be a witness against them from His holy temple.

answers: To flee quickly
To listen carefully
To fight the enemy
medium.q: What does “hearken” mean in this passage?

The testimony has a broad and universal scope
The earth has no connection with the prophecy

The valleys split, and then the Lord returns to His place

The valleys are filled only with water
The mountains melt and the valleys split
challenge.explanation: Together, these images portray a tremendous upheaval of the land.

answers: The transgression of Jacob and the sins of the house of Israel
A drought in the land
A quarrel among the nations

easy.q: What is presented as the reason for the destruction?

answers: It will become a greater city
It will become a heap of the field
It will be moved to Jerusalem

They will be moved to Jerusalem
They will be beaten to pieces

easy.q: What will happen to Samaria’s graven images?

answers: Both are associated with transgression and high places
Both are described as places without sin
Both are rebuilt at the same time
medium.explanation: The passage links Jacob’s transgression with Samaria and Judah’s high places with Jerusalem.
medium.q: What connection is shown between Samaria and Jerusalem?

answers: City gates
Carved idols or images made by human hands
Fields belonging to the city
medium.explanation: A graven image is an idol or carved figure made by people for worship.

They are given to the kings of Judah
They are burned or taken as part of the judgment

The city will expand into new fields
The city will become a trading center

answers: They are collected, rebuilt, and preserved
The images are broken, the hires are burned, and the idols are laid desolate
They are transferred to Judah and made holy

Because it is associated with the transgression of Jacob
Because it is located beside the sea
challenge.explanation: Verse 5 asks, “What is the transgression of Jacob? is it not Samaria?”

paragraphs.title: Lament for Samaria and the Spread of the Wound

answers: He sings a song of victory
He wails and howls
He leaves without speaking
easy.explanation: Micah says, “Therefore I will wail and howl.”
easy.q: How does Micah respond to the coming destruction?

answers: Dragons and owls
Kings and priests
Shepherds and farmers
easy.explanation: His wailing is like that of the dragons and his mourning like that of the owls.
easy.q: To what creatures is Micah’s mourning compared?

answers: Only to Samaria
As far as Egypt
To Judah and the gate of Jerusalem
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says the wound has come unto Judah and the gate of Jerusalem.
easy.q: How far does the wound reach?

answers: It expresses mourning and humiliation
It describes preparation for war
It indicates joy at a feast
medium.explanation: Going stripped and naked is a visible sign of deep grief and disgrace.
medium.q: What does “I will go stripped and naked” reveal about Micah’s condition?

answers: Easy to heal
Extremely severe and not able to be healed
Hidden from everyone
medium.explanation: “Incurable” means the wound is extremely serious and cannot be healed.
medium.q: What does “incurable” mean in “her wound is incurable”?

answers: The wound remains only in Samaria
Judah rescues Samaria
The wound spreads from Samaria to Judah
medium.explanation: The wound does not stop at Samaria but reaches Judah and Jerusalem.
medium.q: What is the relationship between Samaria’s destruction and Judah?

answers: He mourns Samaria’s destruction and its consequences
He describes only his family’s daily life
He celebrates Judah’s victory
challenge.explanation: Micah’s personal grief reflects the destruction of the city and the spread of the judgment.
challenge.q: Why is Micah’s personal lament connected with a national disaster?

answers: The passage moves from a future prophecy to rebuilding
It moves from mourning for Samaria to announcing that the wound has reached Jerusalem
It moves from describing Jerusalem to describing Samaria alone
challenge.explanation: The passage begins with mourning over Samaria and ends with the wound reaching Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What transition occurs between verses 8 and 9?

answers: The intensity and loneliness of the sorrow
The wealth of the land
The strength of the army
challenge.explanation: The comparisons intensify the picture of profound mourning.
challenge.q: What does the comparison with dragons and owls emphasize?

paragraphs.title: The Destruction Moves Through Judah’s Towns

answers: A journey of celebration
A movement of destruction and disaster
A journey of commerce
easy.explanation: The towns are mentioned in connection with shame, mourning, danger, and defeat.
easy.q: What does the sequence of towns describe?

answers: Build new walls
Go out to war
Mourn for her delicate children who have gone into captivity
easy.explanation: Verse 16 calls her to make herself bald and mourn because her children are gone into captivity.
easy.q: What is the daughter of Zion told to do at the end of the passage?

answers: The chariot to the swift beast
The horses to Jerusalem
The camels to Samaria
easy.explanation: Verse 13 says, “bind the chariot to the swift beast.”

answers: Passing through in festival clothing
Being exposed to shame and disgrace
Going armed into battle
medium.explanation: The phrase describes exposure, humiliation, and disgrace.
medium.q: What does “having thy shame naked” mean?

answers: Lachish is called the beginning of the sin of the daughter of Zion
Lachish saves the daughter of Zion
Lachish is rebuilt by the daughter of Zion
medium.explanation: Lachish is described as “the beginning of the sin to the daughter of Zion.”

answers: The spread of disaster through different towns
The division of the land among the tribes
The order of pilgrimage journeys
medium.explanation: Each town is associated with some aspect of shame, mourning, danger, exile, or defeat.
medium.q: What does the sequence of names and commands to the towns convey?

answers: They are woven into a poetic description of disaster and shame
They identify towns that were not affected
They prove that all the towns were built at the same time
challenge.explanation: The town names are used within a poetic series describing grief, disgrace, disappointment, and destruction.
challenge.q: How do the names of the towns function in the prophecy?

answers: The people must send gifts for a festival
The command suggests departure or surrender in the face of disaster
The command announces the building of a new city
challenge.explanation: The command appears in the context of judgment, separation, and the coming loss of the towns.

answers: Joy, victory, and peace
Shame, mourning, insecurity, and finally grief over exile
Curiosity, commerce, and celebration
